recentItems.title: Hudson Valley News Today: Fiery Cornwall crash, flood recovery and an arrest made
recentItems.description:
A Monroe man is recovering after police say his car struck a pole and caught fire in Cornwall when he swerved to avoid another vehicle. Other headlines include the arrest of Ronald Ramirez Rivas following a traffic stop in Carmel, a new agreement to keep school resource officers in the Lakeland School District, bridge repairs causing a closure, and the launch of a new Rockland County emergency preparedness app designed to give residents critical information during emergencies.

recentItems.title: Brooklyn News Today: Police search for suspects in 19 Brooklyn commercial burglaries
recentItems.description:

Meanwhile, a stop-work order remains in place at a Downtown Brooklyn demolition site after heavy equipment reportedly caved into the ground, and a new affordable housing development in Bushwick is providing supportive services for families and formerly homeless residents.

recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Bronx teen stabbed outside school as family mourns Lovay Williams
recentItems.description:

Meanwhile, family members and advocates gathered to honor 27-year-old Lovay Williams following the arrest of 41-year-old Tiliek Thompson, who faces murder, strangulation, assault and child endangerment charges in connection with her death. Other Bronx developments include the death of Highbridge shooting victim Curtis Quinones, a grand larceny investigation in Fordham Heights, and the upcoming opening of Forever After Funeral Services in Wakefield.

recentItems.title: Mayor blames 'computer glitch' for Equinix diesel spill into NJ river
recentItems.description:
A diesel spill released approximately 5,500 gallons of fuel into a tributary of the Hackensack River, with Secaucus Mayor Michael Gonnelli attributing the incident to a “computer glitch.” Equinix says the leak was detected and stopped on Sept. 11, and cleanup crews were immediately deployed. Officials say cleanup is roughly three-quarters complete, with barriers in place to contain the remaining oil. While the New Jersey DEP says no drinking water intake or wildlife impacts have been reported, environmental advocates are raising concerns about broader ecological effects.

recentItems.title: Yankee Stadium among 10 cooling towers linked to South Bronx Legionnaires’ outbreak
recentItems.description:
Yankee Stadium and Lincoln Hospital are among 10 cooling towers that tested positive for Legionella during an investigation into a Legionnaires’ disease outbreak in the South Bronx. Health officials say there are nine confirmed cases, with at least one death and three hospitalizations. While it could take weeks to determine whether live bacteria are present, all 10 locations have been ordered to clean, drain and disinfect their cooling towers.
